title: Add golden fixtures + deterministic tests for Cost Model computations (CI)
author: Leila Farouk
description:
Context
We’re standardizing cost computation primitives so Console + Optimize can consume the same numbers and semantics. To keep Cost Model output stable across runtime/telemetry changes and to prevent regressions (e.g., prefill/decode split, cache-hit attribution, overhead allocation rounding), we need deterministic, versioned golden fixtures and CI enforcement.

This PR adds:
- Golden fixture datasets (JSON) for Cost Model v1 inputs/expected outputs
- Deterministic unit + integration tests that replay fixtures through the library/service computation path
- A CI target that runs the golden suite and fails on drift outside defined tolerances

What’s included
1) Golden fixtures (v1)
- sources live in: cost-model/tests/golden/v1/
- fixtures cover:
  - hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment contexts
  - multiple hardware SKUs (A10/L4/H100 equivalents as represented in model catalog test data)
  - prefill/decode accounting with KV-cache hit/miss
  - batch efficiency variations (single request, small batch, near-capacity batch)
  - quantization profile deltas (baseline fp16, int8 profile id), including explicit “not supported” cases
  - overhead allocation policy buckets (request-attributable vs shared), with finance-aligned rounding rules

2) Deterministic behavior
- normalizes rounding and formatting to avoid flaky snapshot diffs:
  - all monetary values in outputs are asserted in microdollars (USD * 1e6) and rendered consistently
  - uses explicit decimal quantization for percentage fields exposed to Console breakdown tables
- fixes test-time nondeterminism from “current time” inputs by injecting a fixed clock
- pins the fixture runner ordering (stable sort by fixture id)

3) Test runner + CI integration
- new test entrypoint:
  - //cost-model/tests:golden_fixtures_test
- adds CI step (required) to the main pipeline:
  - “cost-model-golden-fixtures”
- adds a documented workflow for updating fixtures (requires two reviewers + explicit rationale in commit message)

Why now
- We’ve already seen drift/regression risk show up in customer-facing differences (SUP-31844, SUP-31877) and internal drift alerts. These tests provide a fast, deterministic guardrail while the telemetry contracts and runtime exports are still evolving.

Implementation notes
- Tolerances:
  - By default, assertions are exact on integer microdollars.
  - For a small subset of fields derived from sampling-based “what-if” projections (not part of this PR’s fixtures), the runner supports a per-field tolerance; for v1 fixtures in this PR, tolerance is set to 0.
- Fixture format:
  - Each fixture includes: schema_version, input, expected_output, and notes.
  - The runner validates schema_version negotiation to ensure we catch accidental breaking changes.

Test plan
- bazel test //cost-model/tests:golden_fixtures_test
- bazel test //cost-model/service/... (ensures service path uses same library computations)
- Verified deterministic output across:
  - local (macOS)
  - linux CI runner

Rollout / risk
- Low runtime risk (tests + fixtures only), but CI will now block merges when cost outputs change.
- Updating goldens requires sign-off from Platform (Ethan) + Telemetry (Nadia/Logan) or Finance (Laura/Rishi) depending on the field impacted.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add “what-if” fixture coverage once ENG-4824 results format stabilizes (include confidence intervals + guardrails).
- Wire a small subset of these fixtures into drift monitoring backtests for early warning (ties into ENG-4827).

Related
- PR #28451 (schema package v1)
- PR #28457 (service endpoints)
- PR #28509 (runtime export for KV cache stats)
- PR #28490 (drift monitoring job)

Checklist
- [x] Fixtures are versioned and include notes + provenance
- [x] Tests deterministic (no wall clock; stable ordering; explicit rounding)
- [x] CI job added and marked required
- [x] Docs added for updating/regenerating fixtures

fixtures(v1): add hosted/dedicated/private datasets incl. kv-cache + batching variants

ci: add required cost-model-golden-fixtures job to main pipeline

review_conversation: Nadia Rahman: Can we avoid floating-point comparisons entirely? Prefill/decode split has been flaky in other repos. If you can assert integer microdollars + integer token counts, we should do that.
Leila Farouk (author): Yep. Updated expected outputs to microdollars and moved token fields to integers everywhere. Also added a guard that fails the runner if it sees NaN/Inf in any computed field.

Thomas Baird: Please add explicit bounds checks in the runner so a malformed fixture can’t accidentally produce an unbounded breakdown (cardinality explosion). Even if it’s “just tests”, it’s a good practice and will mirror service constraints.
Leila Farouk (author): Added a per-fixture max breakdown rows assertion (defaults to 50) and a hard cap in the runner (200) to prevent accidental blowups.
Allison Grant: CI job naming is good, but make sure it’s marked required for main. Also, include a short doc for ‘how to update goldens’ with approval requirements to prevent silent drift.

Leila Farouk (author): Done. Added docs/internal/cost-model/testing/golden-fixtures.md + updated pipeline to required. Also added a check that the PR description includes 'golden update rationale' when any fixture changes.
Rafael Mendes: From SRE perspective, I’m happy with this. One nit: please ensure the fixture runner logs the first diff clearly so the failure is actionable (field path + expected + actual).
Leila Farouk (author): Implemented field-path diff output + prints fixture id + schema version at top of failure. Added an example to the doc.

Ethan Park: Looks good. Requested change: include a dedicated-capacity fixture that exercises the overhead policy buckets explicitly (request-attributable vs shared) with the rounding behavior Finance asked for.
Leila Farouk (author): Added fixture v1/dedicated_overhead_allocation_rounding.json and included explicit notes referencing the policy. Please re-review.
release_notes: Internal: Cost Model now has golden fixture coverage + deterministic CI enforcement to prevent regressions in cost computations used by Console/Optimize.
